SMTO-UI-0045 — Two permission rules give different answers for the same thing

GUID: c68a6279-95d9-4ffc-857d-72214fbcd5e2
Slug: ui-permission-rule-conflict
Domain: UI · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • Your permission settings contain two rules for the same Skill, tool or command, and they disagree, for example one says Allow and the other says Deny. SMTO can't tell which you mean, so it didn't use them.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Select Permissions below the message box. Find the Skill, tool or command the error is about (Technical details may name it) and choose one answer: Allow, Ask or Deny. Choosing a single answer replaces both conflicting rules with one.
  2. Select Apply. This saves the single rule in place of the conflicting pair.
  3. If the window won't open or save, select Use inherited permissions (or Reset to product default for Global), then add back the rules you need. Starting from the usual setup removes the conflicting pair.

What success looks like

  • Apply closes the Permissions window without an error and the rule shows the one answer you chose.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. If someone changes permissions with a script or another tool, ask them to remove the duplicate rule there.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Permission-policy canonicalization found two rules with the same identity (same skill_id, tool_id, or executable plus argv_prefix) but different decisions.

What this means

  • Canonicalization finds two rules with the same identity and different decisions. The shown control rejects this local action before its dependent submission. Earlier requests and saved state are unaffected by this validation result; server-side authority remains authoritative.

Why this can happen

  • Canonicalization finds two rules with the same identity and different decisions.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare normalized identities and decisions rather than merely removing duplicate text.

How to fix it

  • permission_policy.js canonical() throws ui_permission_rule_conflict and AgentPermissionPolicy.canonical_rules raises when rule_identity() collides with a different decision. The editor itself replaces rules by identity, so this usually comes from a stored or API-written policy; remove the duplicate entry and keep a single decision per identity.
  • Remove the conflicting rule and keep one deliberate decision for that identity.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Each identity has one deliberate decision after deduplication.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • The shown control rejects this local action before its dependent submission. Earlier requests and saved state are unaffected by this validation result; server-side authority remains authoritative.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
